channel.description: Latest articles from Lynn Group Media (hoganstand.com)

item.title: Full amalgamation of Laois clubs falls through
item.description: The proposed merger of Laois GAA clubs Ballinakill and Ballypickas has collapsed.

item.title: GAA on TV: All-Ireland and Ulster finals down for decision
item.description: Christmas may only be around the corner, but the big games keep coming in ladies football, camogie and Gaelic football.

item.title: "It would be huge. It would go down in history in our club"
item.description: She has tasted All-Ireland success as a camogie player in the recent past and now Katie Nolan will be hoping to claim national honours with the footballers of Muckalee in Parnell Park tomorrow afternoon.

item.title: Camogie: Gormley and McKernan net early to steer Carrickmore to All-Ireland Junior B title
item.description: First half goals from Sorcha Gormley and Leanne McKernan gave Éire Óg Carrickmore a lead they never relinquished in Abbotstown as the Tyrone side claimed All-Ireland glory at the expense of St Kevin's.

item.title: Camogie: Brídíní Óga clinch second All-Ireland junior crown in three years
item.description: Torie Edgar's accuracy procured a second AIB All-Ireland junior club camogie title for Brídíní Óga Glenravel in three years as they kept St Dominic's resistance under wraps to savour junior glory in windy conditions at Donaghmore Ashbourne GAA grounds this afternoon.

item.title: Ladies: Knockbride storm past Caltra Cuans to All-Ireland intermediate glory
item.description: Sarah McCabe, Gia McCabe and Katie Rogers were amongst the goals at Croke Park as Knockbride became the first team from Cavan to win an AIB All-Ireland intermediate club championship title with a convincing triumph over Galway's Caltra Cuans.

item.title: Ladies: Kilkerrin-Clonberne triumph over Moneyglass to All-Ireland club senior five-in-a-row
item.description: Chloe Miskell and Lynsey Noone grabbed goals in either half at Croke Park on Saturday evening as Kilkerrin-Clonberne defeated St Ergnat's, Moneyglass to earn their fifth AIB All-Ireland Senior Club Championship crown in succession.

item.title: Watch: Kilcoo force extra time against Scotstown with Rodgers point right at the death
item.description: Kilcoo came from eight points down to force extra time in this evening's Ulster club SFC final against Scotstown.

item.title: Scotstown find extra gear against Kilcoo to end 36-year wait for Ulster club SFC glory
item.description: Scotstown triumphed to their fifth Ulster club senior football championship title this evening thanks to a 0-19 to 0-16 extra time victory over Kilcoo at the Box-It Athletic Grounds.
